predictions: Ok, I couldn't have missed that many close matches if I friggin' tried! Last week, I was a lowly 13-11, but a stunning TEN of those 11 losses would have flipped (6 of them) or tied (4 of them) on a single damn dart. I had teams play without their top player(s), a team whose best player left in the middle, another team who added a player, just a lot of stuff that makes this task nigh impossible some weeks. That drops me to 62-34 (64.6% correct) so far, which is… passable, but not awesome.

Match of the week: (G Div.) We're Sexy & We Throw It @ Flight Risks. Alright, G division has played itself into a full haves and have-nots scenario. Three teams undefeated, at least two losses ahead of every other team in the division, less than a full month into the season. And here is round 1 of the battles among that lead trio. We Throw It has a better 301 record, a better SCkt record, a better DCkt record, and they have hit ASPs at a higher rate. So, obviously, I'll take the Risks, 13-11.

Match #2: (D Div.) Dirty Darts Done Dirt Cheap @ Menace 2 Sobriety. Dirty did that thing last week that they seemingly do at least once each season on the way to their division title - they inexplicably dumped a match to a team that came in with a losing record. Yeah, I know that DeMattos isn't playing anymore, but that still doesn't explain why this isn't a battle of undefeateds. Dirty rebounds in a huge match, 14-10.

Match #3: (B Div.) Hump Day! @ Why So Serious? The craziness that is B division (that is now being rivaled by C!) has left us with more than half the division sitting in a lead group of 1-loss teams. It's clear that any B match is big, but those within that lead quarter are likely really big. And this one is that. I'm going with Serious, barely, 13-11.

Match #4: (A Div.) Bully for the Element @ Show Me Your Tips. One of the teams is the most successful team in RDL history. And the other is the real star of the story here. After a week one stumblefest, Show Me promptly dispatched perennial contender Fringe, then torched last season's top newcomer (Attack). Hoping Element avoids the trap, 15-9.

Match #5: (E Div.) Cheap Shots @ Rippin Darts. Neither of this pair has lost a match against a non-top-three team, and they are both still right in the thick of the fight themselves. And while I would love to go Rippin here, I can't until they solve DCkt at least a bit. Cheap, 14-10.

Matches #6 & #7: (C Div.) Darty Little Secrets @ Shooter McGavin; Village Idiots @ One Armed Bandits. The Bandits, averaging only 11 per week, clipped the Wings last week to move to 2-1, and poof, C division is suddenly the tightest, craziest division around (suck it, B division!). It's only 2 matches and 13 points from first to dead last here in C land, so every match every night could be critical. If McGavin and the Idiots win here, it's possible that all but one C team will end the night at 0.500 or below! Sadly, I think the Secrets will handle McGavin, 14-10; but the Bandits will do their part, 13-11.

Match #8: (G Div.) Bright side of Flights @ Game of Throws. The next round in the battle to avoid 'that spot' might be the Game's best shot at their first-ever RDL win. Bright side doesn't comply, 15-9.

Match #9: (A Div.) Dart Attack @ Inconsistently Consistent. The fact that these teams (and especially Attack) are winless just shows the current depth of the A talent spread. Attack gets its first, 16-8.
Match #10: (F Div.) Sofa Kings @ Dart Knights. The Kings play a to-the-last-dart tension fest every single week. The Knights only play near-blowouts, either way. The Knights' system prevails, 15-9.
Match #11: (D Div.) One Dart Wonders @ Darty Sanchez. If Dirty rebounds tonight, the winner here (and both if Sanchez wins) are promptly in the thick of the D title chase. Wonders in a tiebreaker.
Match #12: (F Div.) Death Throw @ Nein Mark. At first glance, this looks like a walk for Death Throw. But Nein has been one dang dart from a win against several good teams. It's DT, but only 13-11.
And the remaining 12 matches, sorted by division:
